description.narrative: Climate Action Network Uganda ( CAN-U) in this project will support the development of integrated policy options for just transition, loss and damage and NDCs through research and a series of dialogues which will also amplify the voice of marginalised and vulnerable communities. The policy dialogues, we include sector coupling to identify what best mix of policies can deliver the best result at the least cost. The project proposes a set of solutions that will facilitate the most marginalized persons to be part of the solution to addressing climate change impacts and associated loss and damage. The solution is anchored on generating strong evidence on the ground through targeted studies in the affected areas where data is collected, analyzed, documented and shared in high level dialogues at national level and international fora. At the center of the policy dialogues, we will do sector coupling to identify what best mix of policies can deliver the best result at least cost. This will be part of the strategy in undertaking studies to support the policy dialogues

participating-org.narrative:
The Climate Action Network Uganda was formed in 2009 by civil society organisations working on climate action in Uganda and beyond.It was formed as a loose network comprising of CSOs, academia, private sector, including individuals. Oxfam GB then hosted the secretariat up to 2016 which then moved to the Ecological Christian Organisation. By 2019, it had become an independent entity, fully registered with the Uganda registration services bureau as a not-for-profit organisation. CAN-U is governed by a Board of Directors who are elected by the Annual General Assembly. The Board of Directors supervises the Technical Secretariat which is headed by the National Coordinator. Currently, CAN-U runs an independent office located on plot 842, Lugolobi Close Ntinda, Kampala. Climate Action Network Uganda (CAN-U) is a registered not-for-profit organisation civil society coalition comprising of Non-Governmental Organizations, Academia, and private sector players working on actions to combat the climate change crisis and its impacts in Uganda.
CAN-U has a membership of about 150 organisations and individuals operating in all the regions of Uganda. They are organized into regional nodes that include: central, east, west, North and Karamoja. Each of these has a lead who represents them on the Board of Directors.
CAN Uganda is affiliated to CAN East Africa, CAN Africa and CAN International.
CAN-U convenes and coordinates civil society in Uganda to rally around the development and implementation of effective climate change policy, legislation and practices at global, national and local levels. We provide the platforms and linkages with key power centres in the climate change space.
CAN-U’s core work is on climate change policy and advocacy that is based on solid evidence gathered through cutting edge research. We mainly work through collaborative partnerships at local, regional, national and international levels where we draw on a highly experienced human resource to support our research.
CAN Uganda represents civil society on key statutory bodies in Uganda. These include: The National Climate Change Advisory Committee, The National Designated Authority, and the technical committee on Green Growth. ACHIEVEMENTS Key areas of initiatives/projects that we have successfully undertaken include: • Promoting participatory Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) for a just transition (supported by CARE German and GIZ) – 2019-2021. This was very instrumental in shaping the current NDCs for Uganda to make sure that they are representative of the voices of the people. • Influencing the formulation of a climate proofed National Forest Policy for Uganda (supported by Forests of the World Denmark) – The network influenced the inclusion of indigenous and forest dependent people’s interests in the policy. This is a positive step towards realizing the rights of these people whohave been marginalized by previous government policies and laws. • Promoting locally led adaptation actions – supported by Oxfam inUganda – 2023 and on-going. This process involves mobilising local communities to implement community tree planting as part of building local level resilience through community forestry. It is also 3. INSTITUTIONAL PURPOSE Mission: Our vision is: ‘A leading network advancing climate change action in Uganda’, while our vision is ‘Actively promoting positive climate change action through advocacy, networking and programme development’.
Institutional objectives: The mission is achieved through the following objectives: i) To undertake resource mobilisation and sustainability for the organisation and her members ii) To enhance organizational strengthening and development iii) To build capacity of members on climate change issues in Uganda and beyond iv) To advocate for effective climate change policy in Uganda that is pro- people v) To Promote research, documentation and information exchange on climate change.
Field(s) of activity: What are the principal thematic and geographic areas in which the organisation works?
In terms of geographical scope, the network works at national level while at regional and international level, we work through our affiliates CAN EasternAfrica and CAN International to advance our positions.
CAN Uganda works on the following programmatic areas. • Governance <(>&<)> Organisational development • Research and capacity development • Thematic Working groups engagement (adaptation, mitigation, gender,technology transfer, loss and damage, finance, policy and legal issues) • Learning, knowledge sharing and Capacity building on climate change • Policy advocacy <(>&<)> Outreach activities on climate change • Membership and partnership development • Resource mobilization • Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning
4. STRATEGIC POSITIONING Analyse the environment in which the organisation works? Who are the other relevant social actors, including government and business, and what roles do they play? ' In this context, what is unique about the position of the organisation? CAN Uganda is a coordinating entity of the civil society in Uganda. Itconvenes, facilitates and influences strategic positions on climate change issues right from local to national level. In this space, we have other actors who include: Environment and Natural resources CSO network who largely work on environment issues, UWASNET who work on water and sanitation, PELUM who work on land use management issues and agroecology, CiSCO who work on issues of oil and gas development. CAN Uganda has built a niche around climate change issues in Uganda and because of this development, legitimacy with the government and stakeholders has been strengthened, We represent CSOs on the National Advisory Committee on Climate Change, the National Designated Authority, the National Task Force on Carbon Markets, the Green Growth Strategy Technical Committee and the Committee on National Climate Finance Strategy. This presents us with the unique position in terms of influencing policy positions and facilitating members to voice their views in these strategic structures
